subject: Is there any way to plot error bars in one facet of time series line graphs?

messages.author: 7dc9525125ca03d3
messages.subject: Is there any way to plot error bars in one facet of time series line graphs?
parts:
I want to print relevant variables for one field season over time.  I'm comparing the amount of north wind, number of moths caught in traps, mass of the local bats, and the number of hours those bats are foraging.  You'll see that some dates are missing for some variables; bats were not sampled every day, for example, but ggplot handles that appropriately when I used na=rm in the melt.   In the code below, the first data frame contains the basic data for all the variables of interest. 

One of these variables is an average (daily bat mass). The second data frame below contains the standard error for bat mass, one of the variables.  Since I've melted the variables, I don't think it is possible to put the std error values into that first melted data frame.

As you can see in the ggplot call at the end, this does in fact produce a graph that's close to what I want.  It would be great if I could somehow add error bars to one of the facets.  Is this at all possible? 
Thanks,
Jennifer
University of Tennessee, Knoxville

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to plot error bars in one facet of time series line graphs?
parts:
Hi Jennifer,

Yep, should be no problem:

sevals$variable <- factor("avgmass",
levels = levels(combo2012$variable))
combo2012 <- merge(combo2012, sevals, all=TRUE)
combo2012 <- within(combo2012, {
lwr <- value - 1.96*massse
upr <- value + 1.96*massse
})

geom_line() +
scale_x_date(limits = c(as.Date("2012-8-16"), as.Date("2012-11-15")))+
facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y")

messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to plot error bars in one facet of time series line graphs?
parts: Woo hoo, awesome, it worked.  Thanks so much!

On Thursday, February 14, 2013 2:18:10 PM UTC-5, izahn wrote:
oops, I just say "error _bars_". Just replace geom_ribbon with
geom_errorbar for that.

Best,
Ista

On Thu, Feb 14, 2013 at 2:16 PM, Ista Zahn <ista...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Jennifer,
>
> Yep, should be no problem:
>
> sevals$variable <- factor("avgmass",
>                           levels = levels(combo2012$variable))
> combo2012 <- merge(combo2012, sevals, all=TRUE)
> combo2012 <- within(combo2012, {
>   lwr <- value - 1.96*massse
>   upr <- value + 1.96*massse
> })
>
> ggplot (data=combo2012, aes(x = date,y=value,group=variable)) +
>   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax=upr)) +
>   geom_line() +
>   scale_x_date(limits = c(as.Date("2012-8-16"), as.Date("2012-11-15")))+
>   facet_grid(variable ~ ., scale = "free_y")
>
> Best,
> Ista
